Jordan — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed MAP milestone for the traffic replay load test so we can align on responsibilities and close timing:

- Recap from call:
  - Goal: validate peak QPS and tail latencies for production traffic using a live traffic replay of May–July 2027 window.
  - Success criteria: 95th percentile < 250ms at customer app-level, no more than 2% error rate at peak.

- Proposed MAP milestone: Traffic replay slotting & capacity sizing
  - Target windows (pick one):
    1) Sep 4–5 (preferred — weekend, low risk)
    2) Sep 11–12 (backup)
  - Redwood responsibilities: reserve burst-capacity hold, provide runbook + ops support, instrument test hooks (KV cache priming and tokenization tracing).
  - FinLytics responsibilities: provide QPS histogram by minute for a representative day, sample traces for 95th tail, and procurement POC to approve dedicated capacity hold.
  - Target close date for MAP milestone: 2027-09-15 (MAP id: DL-8342 / traffic-replay).
  - Dependencies: procurement approval for temporary dedicated capacity, SSO + VPN access for our run engineers, and an agreed runbook for traffic ramping.

Attachments: proposed-map-v1.xlsx (MAP with milestones & owners).

Immediate asks (can we have by EOD Thu?):
- Jordan: share the 7-day QPS histogram (minute granularity) and point me to procurement contact who will sign off on a short reserved capacity hold.
- Marcus: if you can confirm procurement timeline that helps us lock the Sept windows.

I looped in Karthik and Laura to size the replay and own the run. Monica is cc'd for account ops. I’ll follow up internally once we have the histogram.

Thanks,

Adding sizing notes and a preliminary runbook recommendation — feeding off the histogram Jordan attached. Quoted the key lines below for traceability.

Sizing recommendation (preliminary):
- Observed peak 1-min QPS: 8.6k -> recommend reserved capacity hold sized to ~2x observed peak for safety during replay (allowing for bursts and parallelism) -> target reserved peak capacity equivalent to ~17k QPS.
- Suggested hardware: 6 x a2-highmem-like nodes with continuous batching and KV-cache enabled (we'll refine after we get sample payload sizes). For dedicated capacity we can also use 4 larger nodes + 2 burst nodes.

Runbook & ramp plan (high level):
1) Prep (day -7): credentials, SSH + VPN, SSO test, priming KV cache.
2) Dry run (day -1): small scale 10% volume replay to validate throughput and monitoring.
3) Main replay (day 0): step ramp 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% over ~90 minutes. Monitor 95th latency and error rates; abort if 95th > 350ms or error > 4%.
4) Cooldown & post-analysis (day +1): gather traces, tokenization variance, and cost estimation.

Telemetry asks (Jordan please share):
- Typical prompt / message token length distribution (csv sample)
- 95th tail latency targets at app layer
- Any request batching patterns or long-running streaming sessions that replay should avoid

I've attached a short runbook draft (replay-runbook-v0.3.md) that the ops team can iterate on. Laura — can you own the run coordination and confirm your on-call coverage for the weekend windows? Monica — can you own the procurement coordination with Marcus?
